paragraphs: GovShield sells an artificial intelligence platform built for law enforcement agencies. The pitch is ChatGPT-like capabilities for reports, records, and administrative work. The company sums up its own positioning as secure AI designed by cops, for cops.

Its agents review reports, warrants, and more for clarity, content, and legal compliance. Redaction of license plates, names, and addresses is described as automatic and switchable. Agency data can be queried to create crime maps and understand trends. Report databases can also be queried to fulfil Public Records Act requests. On security, the site claims strict compliance with CJIS Security Policy 5.9 and hosting on Microsoft Azure Government Cloud.

Individual users can sign up for a trial without an agency contract. Signing up an entire agency is priced at $29 per user per month. The founder, Nate Horton, is described as a U.S. Army combat veteran and a law enforcement professional with over a decade of experience. The platform is built on Mendix, a low-code platform owned by Siemens.

quote.text: Is AI Safe to Use in Law Enforcement?
